# Functional Design — Airflow Workflows (Platform DAG Factory)

Current functional design of the platform component that turns data product repositories into Airflow DAGs. For architecture, see [`../application-design.md`](../application-design.md). History is in the [Platform DAG Factory intent archive](../../../archive/20261110-platform-dag-factory/intent-summary.md); the checkpoint key mount is from the [Spark S3 Checkpoints intent archive](../../../archive/20261111-spark-s3-checkpoints/intent-summary.md).

## Responsibility
`infra/airflow/lakehouse_dags` builds every data product's DAGs from the product repository's `workflows/*.json`, and supplies all the task code those DAGs run.

| A product repository holds | The platform holds |
|---|---|
| `workflows/<project>/<name>.json` (or flat `workflows/<name>.json`), one DAG each | DAG construction, the task callables, and the JSON rules |
| `notebooks/` (workload entry points and the `common/` helpers, also used by Jupyter) | The Spark container lifecycle, the broker registration, renewal and revocation, and redaction |
| `configs/<env>.yml`, optional `configs/<product>/<env>.yml` | The CI validator |
| `dags/lakehouse.py`, the fixed stub (`spec.STUB_TEXT`) | |

**Deployment**:
- `airflow-dag-processor` and `airflow-scheduler` mount `./infra/airflow/lakehouse_dags` read-only at `/opt/lakehouse/python/lakehouse_dags`, with `PYTHONPATH=/opt/lakehouse/python`.
- Jenkins mounts the same package plus `infra/jenkins/bin/lakehouse-validate-workflows`.
- Changes are visible through the mount at once. Apply them with `start-airflow`, after `scripts/verify/dag-factory-tests.sh`.
- `airflow-scheduler` (which runs the tasks, LocalExecutor) also mounts the staged checkpoint keys `.runtime/container-mounts/checkpoint-keys` read-only at `/run/secrets/checkpoint-keys`; every Airflow service gets `LAKEHOUSE_CHECKPOINT_KEYS_HOST_DIR`, the same folder's host path, exported by `scripts/lakehouse.sh`.

## Modules
| Module | Dependencies | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `__init__` | lazy | `load_workflows(namespace, stub_file)` |
| `spec` | standard library | Workflow JSON v1: `parse_workflow`, `to_document`, `load_repository`, `check_repository`, `STUB_TEXT` |
| `identity` | standard library | bundle name from the checkout path, then `(bundle, product, environment)` |
| `factory` | Airflow, Docker SDK | `build_dag`, `LakehouseOperator`, and the task callables |
| `redact` | standard library | `redact_spark_output` |
| `mv_deploy` | standard library (+ pymysql to connect) | materialized-view promotion: `render`, `deployable`, `plan`, `apply`, `connect` (see `materialized-view-promotion.md`) |
| `task_args` | standard library | trigger-time task arguments: `check_task_args`, `task_values`, `effective_args`, `option_name` |
| `validate` | standard library | `python3 -m lakehouse_dags.validate [ROOT]` |

## Rules
- **Workflow file**: `workflows/<name>.json` or, per subproject, `workflows/<project>/<name>.json` (`<project>` matching `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,49}`, one level), a JSON object, in UTF-8. Only `*.json` files belong in `workflows/` and its subproject folders; invalid folder names, deeper folders and other files are problems; hidden entries are ignored. A workflow name is unique across the repository (DAG IDs don't include the subproject); a repeated name is a problem naming both files.
  - `apiVersion`: exactly `lakehouse.local/workflow/v1`.
  - `name`: `[a-zA-Z0-9_-][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,99}`, equal to the file stem.
  - `schedule`: required; `null`, or a string of 1 to 100 printable characters.
  - `description`: optional, 1 to 500 printable characters.
  - `tags`: optional, at most 10 distinct tags matching `[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]{1,50}`; `spark` is reserved.
  - `tasks`: 1 to 50 tasks.
  - Unknown keys are refused, and booleans are never integers.
- **Task**:
  - `name`: same pattern as the workflow name, unique.
  - `entrypoint`: `[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\.py`, optionally prefixed by a layer folder `bronze/`, `silver/`, `gold/`, `ops/`, `deploy/` or `other/` (one level, no `..`), existing in the workflow's code folder: `notebooks/workload/<project>/` for a subproject workflow, `notebooks/workload/` for a flat one (`Workflow.entrypoint_path`).
  - `runs_after`: distinct names of existing tasks, no self-reference, no cycle.
  - `args`: at most 50 strings, each 1 to 500 printable characters.
  - `retries` 0 to 10; `retry_delay_seconds` 0 to 3600, only with `retries` ≥ 1; `execution_timeout_seconds` 1 to 86400.
  - Unknown keys are refused.
- **Identity**:
  - **Bundle name**: the parent of the nearest `tracking_repo` or `versions` directory above the stub.
  - **Accepted**: only `<product>-main` (environment `prod`) and `<product>-uat` (`uat`), with the product matching `[a-z][a-z0-9]{1,19}`. Anything else is an import error; legacy `lakehouse-*` and `dev` are not accepted.
- **DAG**:
  - **Settings**: `dag_id` is `<bundle>-<name>`; tags are `{<bundle>, spark, *tags}`; `start_date` 2024-01-01 UTC; `catchup` false; `rerun_with_latest_version` false. The description defaults to the task list.
  - **Tasks**: `create_cluster`, then `install_requirements` (2 retries, 30 s apart), then `validate_environment`, then `submit_<task>` (after its `runs_after` predecessors, or after `validate_environment`), then `stop_cluster` (`ALL_DONE`), then `verify_workloads_succeeded`.
  - **Task options**: `retries`, `retry_delay` and `execution_timeout` are set on that task's `submit_` only.
  - **Trigger-time task arguments**: every DAG has one param, `task_args` (`Param({}, type="object")`, description with an example and the task names): `{"<task>": {"<argument>": "<value>"}}`. Task names must be the workflow's; argument names `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}`; values printable strings of 1 to 500 characters; at most 20 per task. Airflow doesn't check the object's content (probe P1), so the factory does.
- **Task code**:
  - **Templates**: every task is a `LakehouseOperator` (`template_fields = ()`), so `{{ conn.* }}` and `{{ var.* }}` in `args` are never rendered.
  - **Checkpoint key** (`_checkpoint_key_volume`, before the broker registration): the bucket of the run's product and environment comes from `/run/secrets/checkpoint-keys/.buckets.json` (product → environment → bucket, no secrets, written by the RustFS checkpoint key bootstrap, because the scheduler has no product model). The staged file must be a regular file, not a symlink; the host folder must be absolute and named `checkpoint-keys`. It becomes the one read-only mount `/run/secrets/lakehouse-checkpoints/<bucket>`, so a `-main` run holds only the `prod` key and a `-uat` run only the `uat` key. Any problem fails `create_cluster` before a run is registered or a container exists.
  - **`create_cluster`**: first checks the run's `task_args` (all problems in one error, before the checkpoint key, the broker registration or any container); then registers `{dag_id, run_id}` with the broker over the pinned endpoint and CA. It starts `lakehouse-<dag_id[:40]>-<sha256(run_id)[:12]>` with the run's bundle checkout at `/opt/lakehouse-bundle` (read-only), the broker CA and the checkpoint key. The environment holds the token, run handle and capability, `LAKEHOUSE_ENVIRONMENT`, `LAKEHOUSE_PRODUCT`, and `PYTHONPATH=/opt/lakehouse-bundle`. If startup fails, it removes the container and revokes the run.
  - **`install_requirements`**: an `exec_run` in that container of `/opt/lakehouse/venv/bin/python /opt/lakehouse/workload_python.py install-extras /opt/lakehouse-bundle/requirements.txt --lock /opt/lakehouse/requirements.lock`: nothing without the file; otherwise the extras, constrained by the lock, into the container's venv, with the output redacted (rules in `workload-python-environment.md`).
  - **`validate_environment`**: an `exec_run` in that container of `/opt/lakehouse/venv/bin/python -c` with the repository's `notebooks/common/config_loader.load_environment_config(env, /opt/lakehouse-bundle/configs, product)`.
  - **`submit_<task>`**: `spark-submit --master <LAKEHOUSE_SPARK_MASTER> /opt/lakehouse-bundle/notebooks/workload/[<project>/]<entrypoint> --environment <env> --config-dir /opt/lakehouse-bundle/configs`, then `--` and the effective arguments when there are any: the workflow `args` with the run's `task_args` for this task applied (each value one `--<name>=<value>` token appended; the same option, as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`, removed from the workflow `args` first). Both lists are logged (redacted). Arguments are passed as a list, and the output is redacted.
  - **`stop_cluster`**: removes the container and revokes the broker run.
- **Repository code never runs in the scheduler**: it runs only inside the run's Spark container. At parse time, the dag-processor imports only files under `dags/` (the bundles' `subdir`): the stub, and any other `.py` file a repository might add there, which CI refuses.
- **Loading**: `load_workflows` validates every file first.
  - **Problems**: any problem raises one `WorkflowError` listing `<path>: <field>: <message>` for all of them, so no DAG of that bundle loads.
  - **No workflows**: without `workflows/`, or with no workflow files, nothing is built and nothing fails.
- **Validator** (`check_repository`): the workflow rules, plus `dags/lakehouse.py` must equal `STUB_TEXT` (line endings normalized) and `dags/` may hold nothing else (`__pycache__` excepted). Exit 0 prints `OK: <n> workflow(s)`; exit 1 prints the problems and `N problem(s)`; exit 2 means a usage error. The Jenkins wrapper `lakehouse-validate-workflows` then checks a root `requirements.txt`, when present, with `workload_python.py check-extras`; it exits 1 if either check fails.
- **Bundle checkouts**: `sparse_dirs` is `dags`, `workflows`, `notebooks`, `configs`, `materialized_views`; Git's cone mode also checks out every root file, such as `requirements.txt`. `subdir` is `dags`, so Airflow's DAG folder is `dags/`, while the stub still takes the repository root from its own path. Airflow applies `sparse_dirs` only at the first clone, so `scripts/setup/sync-bundle-checkouts.py`, run by `start-airflow` before Airflow starts, updates each configured bundle's `tracking_repo` when its sparse list differs.
- **Repository-side contract** (`opensource-lakehouse-sample-dp` from `42de0f3`):
  - `notebooks/common/config_loader.py` provides `load_environment_config(environment, config_dir, product)`; configs are repository-owned and free-form, every key reaches the job; `configs/<product>/<env>.yml` is used in Airflow only.
  - Entry points accept `--environment` and `--config-dir`; `notebooks.common.job_runtime.start_spark_job(app_name)` returns `(spark, config)` through the platform's `lakehouse_spark` (see `workload-python-environment.md`).
  - Task arguments: `notebooks.common.cli.parse_task_args(declaration)`; names map to options (`scale_factor` → `--scale-factor`, `--opt value` or `--opt=value`); spec `required` or a string `default`; values are strings, never checked by the parser; structural problems are reported together with the usage and exit 2 (Airflow) or raise `TaskArgumentError` (Jupyter). In Jupyter the values come from the notebook's widgets (`notebooks/common/jupyter_input_widget_helper.py`, from `WIDGET_LIST`), else its `TASK_ARGS`; `task_args()` returns the raw list.
  - `opensource-lakehouse-sample-dp` (from `f8c13e0`) uses subproject `sample`: `workflows/sample/`, notebooks in `notebooks/workload/sample/other/`, entry points `other/<file>.py`; its AGENTS.md describes the subproject and layer layout.
  - Notebooks have the sections Initialization (`# !lakehouse-install-requirements ~/work/opensource-lakehouse-sample-dp`, `# %run ../../../common/jupyter_environment_resolver.py` from a layer folder), Imports, their own sections, and Execution (only the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block, so importing a notebook runs nothing). The resolver uses `dev` unless `LAKEHOUSE_ENVIRONMENT` is `uat` or `prod`, and names the Spark application `<env>-<notebook>`.

## Failure behavior
- **Invalid workflow**: an import error naming every problem; the bundle has no DAGs until it's fixed.
- **Non-product bundle**: an import error.
- **Config check fails**: `validate_environment` fails with redacted output, then `stop_cluster` cleans up.
- **Invalid `task_args`**: `create_cluster` fails naming every problem; nothing is registered or started.
- **Broker refusal**: `create_cluster` fails (`unknown_product`, `unknown_dag`, `bundle_mismatch`), with no fallback identity.
- **Checkpoint key missing or unsafe** (no index entry, missing or symlinked file, bad host folder or bucket name): `create_cluster` fails naming the bucket and the product bootstrap; nothing is registered or started. `start-airflow` refuses to start while any product bucket lacks a staged key.
- **Observed once (2026-11-10)**: Airflow's per-task bundle refresh hit "detected dubious ownership" on `tracking_repo` when two tasks started together. It did not repeat, and the cause is not established.

## Verification and limits
- **Verified 2026-11-11 (MV promotion)**: workflow DAGs of a bundle with views run `deploy_materialized_views` after `validate_environment` and before the tasks; `<bundle>-deploy_materialized_views` exists only when the branch has view files; a live `tpch_medallion` UAT run deployed as its first step. Rules in `materialized-view-promotion.md`.
- **Verified 2026-11-11 (task parameters)**: host 608 passed, Airflow image 81 passed (param on every DAG; invalid `task_args` fail before registration or container; values reach only their task; property: render-then-parse gives trigger values once, workflow values otherwise). Live UAT: `{"tpch_region_load": {"silver_lookback_days": "1"}}` gave that task `--silver-lookback-days=1` (`lookback_days` 1), others unchanged; an unknown task and a non-string value failed at `create_cluster` with no container.
- **Verified 2026-11-11 (Spark S3 checkpoints)**: host `tests/airflow` 71 passed (one key per environment; missing, symlinked, unindexed, unknown-product, bad host folder and bad bucket cases fail before registration); `default-uat-test_environment` 8/8 with only `/run/secrets/lakehouse-checkpoints/bucket-default-uat` (ro) mounted.
- **Verified 2026-11-10 (shared workload requirements)**: Airflow image 51 passed (the `install_requirements` task, its command and retries, redaction); `default-uat-test_environment` 8/8 without extras; `default-uat-generate_tpch` 13/13 with extras; with `subdir`, only `dags/lakehouse.py` is parsed per bundle.
- **Verified 2026-11-10 (DAG factory)**:
  - host suite 458 passed (P1, P3, P4; spec, validator, wiring, checkout sync);
  - 49 passed in the Airflow image (golden DAG, platform-only callables, no templating, ported container, broker and cleanup tests, P2);
  - workload repository 36 passed (P5);
  - live: both `default` DAGs built from the stub with unchanged IDs, a UAT run 7 of 7 (after one transient failure), and Jenkins `default_ci` with the validation stage.
- **Verified 2026-11-11 (workflow subprojects)**: host 547 and Airflow image 71 passed (P5: round-trip of mixed flat and subproject repositories; layer entry points); flat, subproject and `other/` layouts each loaded the same four DAGs; UAT 8/8 and 13/13 on `1b83568` and `f8c13e0`; Jenkins `default_ci` #11 and #12.
- **Verified 2026-11-10 (Spark session helper)**: UAT runs on `ad1ca8d`, `41ee812`, `42de0f3` (8/8, 13/13 each; `--entity` through `parse_task_args`; application `uat-test_environment`); Jenkins `default_ci` for each.
- **User-confirmed after closure (2026-11-10)**: an interactive JupyterHub run of the notebooks on the new image.
- **Not run**: a production run; a CI refusal on a pushed invalid branch.
- **Limits**:
  - parse-time execution of extra repository `.py` files until an enforcing bundle class exists (later phase);
  - single-container `local[*]` Spark;
  - no templating in `args` or `task_args`;
  - anyone who may trigger a DAG may set `task_args` (Airflow roles are platform-wide);
  - workload code runs on the shared Python 3.10 environment plus the repository's `requirements.txt` (see `workload-python-environment.md`).

# Functional Design — StarRocks SQL Access

This is the current functional design of the StarRocks component. For architecture, see [`../application-design.md`](../application-design.md); for the product access model, see [`lakehouse-product-access.md`](lakehouse-product-access.md). History is in the [StarRocks Integration](../../../archive/20261109-starrocks-integration/intent-summary.md) [Data Product and User Scripts](../../../archive/20261109-data-product-and-user-scripts/intent-summary.md), [StarRocks LDAP Login](../../../archive/20261109-starrocks-ldap-login/intent-summary.md), and [StarRocks Metadata Access](../../../archive/20261111-starrocks-metadata-access/intent-summary.md) intent archives.

## Responsibility
StarRocks 4.1.7 gives people and tools interactive SQL over every data product's Iceberg tables in Polaris, with access identical to each product's roles. It also hosts materialized views in internal databases. It owns no source data: tables live in Polaris and RustFS.

## Catalogs and databases
The three external catalogs are shared by all products. Each product's namespaces appear as databases in them, and each product has its own MV databases in `default_catalog`. For `default`:

| Environment | External catalog (Iceberg REST, Polaris warehouse) | Database (namespace) | Internal MV database (`default_catalog`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| prod | `lakehouse` | `default_lh` | `default_lh` |
| uat | `lakehouse_uat` | `default_lhuat` | `default_lhuat` |
| dev | `lakehouse_dev` | `default_lhdev` | `default_lhdev` |

Catalog properties:
- `type=iceberg`, `iceberg.catalog.type=rest`, and `iceberg.catalog.uri=http://polaris:8181/api/catalog`, with the warehouse set to the catalog name.
- `iceberg.catalog.security=oauth2`, with `oauth2.credential=srv-starrocks:<secret>`, `oauth2.server-uri` set to the Keycloak token endpoint at `keycloak:8080`, `oauth2.scope=openid`, and `oauth2.token-refresh-enabled=true`.
- `iceberg.catalog.vended-credentials-enabled=true`.
- `aws.s3.endpoint=http://rustfs:9000`, path-style access, and region `us-east-1`. No storage keys.

## Access model (mirrors Polaris)
- **Roles**: each product group maps to the role with underscores (`role-sales-owner` → `role_sales_owner`). Its levels come from the product file's `access` (catalog databases) and `materialized_views` (MV databases), on that product's databases only.
- **Default matrix** (`data-products/default.yaml`, also the template):

  | Role | prod | uat | dev | MV databases (prod / uat / dev) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `role_default_owner` | manage | manage | manage | manage / manage / manage |
  | `role_default_developer` | read | read | write | read / read / author |
  | `role_default_analyst` | read | none | none | read / none / none |
  | `role_default_writer` | write | write | write | author / author / author |
  | `role_platform_admin` | manage (catalog-wide) | manage (catalog-wide) | manage (catalog-wide) | manage in every product |

- **Levels**, in catalog `c` for the product database `d`:
  - **every level but `none`** also gets `SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN DATABASE information_schema` in `c` (see "Catalog metadata" below)
  - **read**: `USAGE ON CATALOG c`, `SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN DATABASE d`
  - **write**: read, plus `INSERT ON ALL TABLES IN DATABASE d` and `CREATE TABLE ON DATABASE d`. No drop, delete, alter, or `CREATE DATABASE`.
  - **manage**: `USAGE ON CATALOG c`, `ALL ON DATABASE d`, `ALL ON ALL TABLES IN DATABASE d`
  - **platform admin**: `ALL` on the catalog, all databases, and all tables
- **MV levels**:
  - **MV read**: `SELECT ON ALL MATERIALIZED VIEWS IN DATABASE d`
  - **MV author**: MV read plus `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ON DATABASE d`, and `ALTER`, `REFRESH`, and `DROP` on its materialized views
  - **MV manage**: `ALL` on the database and its materialized views
- **Built-ins**: platform admins also get `user_admin`, `db_admin`, and `cluster_admin`.
- **Visibility**: a user sees only the databases they have privileges on.
- **Catalog metadata** (since 2026-11-11): StarRocks 4.1.7 checks `SELECT` on an external catalog's `information_schema` tables, which SQL clients (DBeaver's MySQL driver) query to list tables and columns; without it, product users got error 5203 ("SELECT privilege(s) on TABLE tables") although `SHOW TABLES` and queries worked. Every product role with `USAGE` on a catalog therefore holds `SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN DATABASE information_schema` there (`METADATA_DATABASE` in the bootstrap). The rows are filtered by the user's own privileges: a role with only this grant sees no table of any product (probed, and verified in Build and Test), so the shared catalogs reveal nothing across products. Platform admins already hold `ALL` on the catalogs.
- **Polaris is the outer bound.** The shared catalog identity `srv-starrocks` is in every product's writer group, so drops through StarRocks are refused by Polaris, even for manage-level roles. Polaris's read set includes `NAMESPACE_READ_PROPERTIES`, because StarRocks loads namespace metadata when it opens a database.
- **2026-11-09 migration of `default`**: catalog-wide grants were replaced by database-scoped ones. Writers and owners lost `CREATE DATABASE` on the catalogs, and developers gained MV authoring in dev (CR-2).

## Role enforcement (`infra/starrocks/bootstrap-starrocks.py`)
- It creates missing managed roles and every product's MV databases, and grants every privilege of the product files again. `GRANT` is idempotent, and StarRocks reports `ALL` as individual privileges, so some grants are reissued on each run (27 for `default`).
- Additions run before revocations.
- **Database-scoped forms**: `ALL TABLES IN DATABASE d` is parsed and rendered alongside the existing forms.
- **Options**: `--product FILE` validates a file (the roles always follow every file). `--inventory` prints a product's MV-database object counts. `--remove [--purge-data]` drops a product's MV databases (`FORCE`; refused while they hold objects without purge) and roles, then converges the platform admin over the remaining products.
- It revokes, and reports by name, managed-role privileges the matrix does not cover. A privilege is covered when it is desired, or when `ALL` is desired on the same object.
- A grant form it cannot parse is reported for manual review and never revoked. Roles and users it does not manage are never changed.
- Catalogs: a missing catalog is created. An existing one is compared without its masked credential: equal means no change, and a difference stops the run with nothing changed, naming only the catalog. `--recreate-catalogs` drops and recreates all three, for secret rotation or repair, with no data loss.
- `--runtime-only` (core start):
  - **Root password**: kept if root logs in with the file password. Set from the file if root logs in with an empty one (a fresh FE). Otherwise it refuses.
  - **Backend**: registers `starrocks-be:9050` and waits until it is alive. In 4.1.7 the host is read from the `IP` column.

## Users (`infra/starrocks/reconcile-starrocks-users.py`)
- **Desired users**: every enabled Keycloak user in at least one group of any product file, except `service-account-*` users. Roles are the union of their groups' roles, plus the built-ins for platform admins.
- **Managed users and login methods**: people log in with LDAP (`IDENTIFIED WITH authentication_ldap_simple`); each product's writer user (`writer_user.username`) logs in with its Keycloak access token (`IDENTIFIED WITH authentication_jwt AS '{"jwks_url": "http://keycloak:8080/realms/lakehouse/protocol/openid-connect/certs", "principal_field": "preferred_username", "required_issuer": "http://keycloak.localhost:8080/realms/lakehouse"}'`; `STARROCKS_JWT_JWKS_URL`, `KEYCLOAK_ISSUER` override). A user on the wrong method is **switched in place** with `ALTER USER … IDENTIFIED WITH …`, which keeps its grants and the materialized views it owns. Both plugins count as managed for drops.
- **Apply order**: create, switch, grant, revoke, `SET DEFAULT ROLE ALL`, then drop managed users who left every product group. A native-password user with a desired name is a conflict: it is reported and left unchanged. `root` and built-in users are never managed.
- **Bind pattern**: after its safety checks, every run re-applies the LDAP bind pattern if the FE lost it (an FE restart resets this runtime setting). `--bind-pattern-only` does only that, with the root login and no Keycloak read or product validation; the scheduled cycle runs it first (since 2026-11-11), so logins recover even while the user sync is refused.
- **Safety**:
  - If Keycloak is unreadable or returns no product-group members, nothing changes and the exit code is non-zero.
  - If any managed role is missing, nothing changes. This happens when the scheduled run precedes the product bootstrap.
  - **Except** for products being removed: a product group missing from Keycloak counts as empty, and its roles are no longer required.
  - If a product file is invalid, nothing changes.
  - The scheduled image provides Python, pinned PyYAML and the MariaDB client; the product model, both reconcile scripts, `starrocks_common.py` and `run.sh` are mounted read-only from the repository (since 2026-11-11: a baked-in copy of an older model had refused every cycle with `unknown keys: repo`), and `data-products/` likewise.
- **When it runs**: in the product bootstrap; on demand with `lakehouse.sh reconcile-starrocks` (the `docker exec` transport); and on the scheduled `polaris-group-reconciler` cycle (network transport: the MariaDB client connects with `--ssl --ssl-verify-server-cert` and the StarRocks CA mounted at `/run/certs/starrocks-ca.crt`; skipped when StarRocks is disabled).
- **MV authorship**: a dropped user's materialized views may stop refreshing; an owner or platform admin must re-create them.

## Login
- **Method**: people log in with their own username and LDAP password; product writers only with a Keycloak token (the materialized-view deploy; see `materialized-view-promotion.md`). People use the same password as for Keycloak. One StarRocks user has exactly one login method (probed), so the former token login was retired: the `starrocks` Keycloak client and `scripts/clients/starrocks-token.sh` are gone.
- **TLS**: the FE serves the SQL port with a certificate from a local CA (SAN `starrocks-fe`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`), made by `scripts/setup/prepare-starrocks-certificates.py`. `ssl_force_secure_transport = true` refuses every plain-text connection, root included. This matters because the client sends the password in clear text inside the TLS session (`mysql_clear_password`).
- **Password check**: the FE binds to LDAP over LDAPS (`ldap:636`, `ssl_conn_allow_insecure = false`, trust store `/run/certs/ldap-ca.crt`) as `uid=${USER},ou=people,dc=lakehouse,dc=local`, so StarRocks holds no LDAP credential.
  - **Where the pattern is set**: it is a runtime setting. `fe.conf` would expand `${USER}` as an environment variable ("no such env variable: USER") and the FE would refuse to start, so `bootstrap-starrocks.py --runtime-only` sets it at every start and the user sync re-applies it.
- **Command line**: `scripts/clients/starrocks-login.sh [--password-file FILE] <user>` uses a `mysql:9.7.2` container with `--enable-cleartext-plugin` and `--ssl-mode=VERIFY_IDENTITY` against the StarRocks CA. Service users use their password file under `.runtime/credentials/`.
- **JDBC, DBeaver, and BI tools**: username and password with `sslMode=REQUIRED`, or `VERIFY_IDENTITY` with a truststore of the StarRocks CA. Connector/J 9.3.0 was verified with both; `DISABLED` is refused.
- **Browsing in SQL clients**: leave the connection's default database empty (the session starts in `default_catalog`, whose `default_lh`, `default_lhuat` and `default_lhdev` are the materialized-view databases, not the Iceberg namespaces; DBeaver may draw them under whichever node is open). Iceberg tables are browsed in the catalogs or named `catalog.database.table`. Users reconnect after a grant change, because roles are read at login.
- **Secret handling**: the password is read without echo or from a file, and reaches the client container only through `MYSQL_PWD` (copied by `docker run -e`). Nothing secret is printed or put in arguments. Host-side SQL passes the root password through `MYSQL_PWD`, copied by `docker exec -e`, never as an argument.

## Opt-out and failure behavior
- **`STARROCKS_ENABLED=false`** (environment or `.env`; case-insensitive): start, status, and stop leave out the StarRocks file. Both scripts print a notice and exit 0. The scheduled cycle skips StarRocks.
- **Enabled but unreachable**: the product bootstrap and on-demand reconcile fail with exit 1. The scheduled cycle logs the failure and retries.
- **LDAP unavailable**: new password logins fail (LDAP bind); open sessions continue.
- **Keycloak unavailable**: SQL logins keep working (they depend on LDAP only), but catalog token renewal to Polaris fails until Keycloak returns.
- **FE restarted outside `lakehouse.sh start`**: password logins fail ("empty password is not allowed for simple authentication") until the next scheduled cycle's bind-pattern step (at most one interval, 300 s by default), or `reconcile-starrocks-users.py --bind-pattern-only` on the host at once.

## Testable properties (Hypothesis; partial PBT mode)
- P1: catalog properties round-trip through render and parse.
- P2: JWT users are switched in place, never recreated or dropped while desired.
- P3: grants equal the matrix for each role and environment.
- P4: applying a grant plan covers the matrix and leaves unmanaged roles alone.
- P5: desired users follow groups and exclude service accounts.
- P6: applying a user plan leaves every desired user with its login method (token for writers, LDAP for people) and exactly its roles; native-password users are never changed (P2b re-plans to no switch).

- P9: a role holds the `information_schema` metadata grant on a catalog exactly when it holds `USAGE` there, only as `SELECT`, never on the database itself.

The tests are in `tests/starrocks/`.

# Application Design — Keycloak, Polaris, RustFS, Jenkins, StarRocks, and Console/UI SSO

## Purpose

This project provides a local Docker Compose lakehouse platform. It hosts one or more **data products**, each described by one YAML file in `data-products/` (`default` is the first and cannot be removed). Legacy Hive or FreeIPA state is not migrated. For every product it provisions:

- identity groups and a writer user
- storage buckets
- namespaces in the shared Polaris catalogs
- namespace- and database-scoped authorization grants
- RustFS console policies
- app mappings (JupyterHub, Airflow, Jenkins)

The product bootstrap also creates Spark smoke tables for `default` across production, dev, and UAT.

## Components

- **Keycloak** provides the `lakehouse` OIDC realm, four groups per data product plus `role-platform-admin`, five bootstrap users, one writer user per product, the `lakehouse-writer` workload client, the `srv-starrocks` catalog service account, and browser-login clients for JupyterHub, Airflow, the RustFS console, and Jenkins. Users and passwords are stored in the LDAP directory through the writable `lakehouse-ldap` provider; groups stay in Keycloak. See `functional-design/lakehouse-product-access.md`.
- **LDAP directory** (`ldap`, OpenLDAP 2.6.8 from pinned Alpine 3.22 packages, `infra/ldap/`):
  - **Holds**: the users and passwords shared by Keycloak and StarRocks.
  - **Access**: LDAPS only (636) plus a local `ldapi` socket for the healthcheck, Argon2 password hashes, no host port, on the `core` network only.
  - **Tree**: `dc=lakehouse,dc=local`, with `ou=people` (users, `uid` = username) and `ou=services` (`cn=keycloak`, the only identity allowed to write `ou=people`).
  - **Seeding**: an empty volume is seeded once, and the Keycloak bind hash is refreshed from its protected file at every start.
- **Apache Polaris** provides Iceberg REST and management APIs, catalogs, namespaces, principal roles, grants, and scoped RustFS credential vending.
- **PostgreSQL** stores Keycloak and Polaris state in separate databases and named volumes.
- **RustFS** (1.0.4) provides S3-compatible storage: three environment buckets per data product. Bootstrap creates missing resources and preserves existing objects. Its console accepts Keycloak OIDC sign-in, with root static keys kept as break-glass. Each bucket also has a checkpoint user `ckpt-<bucket>` limited to its `checkpoints/` prefix (see [Streaming checkpoints](#streaming-checkpoints)).
- **Host scripts** (`scripts/`): the entry points `lakehouse.sh` (start, status, stop, reset, StarRocks reconcile, Airflow commands) and `bootstrap-default-product.sh`, plus helpers grouped by purpose in `setup/`, `bootstrap/`, `operations/`, `clients/`, and `verify/`. `operations/` holds the operator commands `create-data-product.sh`, `remove-data-product.sh`, and `create-user.sh` (see [Data products](#data-products)).
- **Data product model** (`infra/products/`): `data_products.py` loads and validates the product files and derives names. `template.yaml` is the `--init` template, `render_jenkins.py` renders the Jenkins configuration, product folders and jobs, and `product-cli.py` holds the operator helpers. Every component reads the files through this module.
- **Apache Airflow** provides the production/UAT workload control plane and browser UI. It uses FAB authentication through Keycloak, with a local administrator recovery login. The platform DAG factory `infra/airflow/lakehouse_dags` (mounted read-only into the dag-processor and the scheduler) builds every product's DAGs from its repository's `workflows/*.json`; see `functional-design/airflow-workflows.md`.
- **Spark** runs on-demand Iceberg workloads using workload-specific OAuth identities and Polaris-vended S3 credentials; Structured Streaming checkpoints use `s3ckpt://` on Hadoop S3A with a per-bucket checkpoint key.
- **JupyterHub** remains a separately supported interactive service with user-bound Spark authentication. User servers run as the Jupyter Docker Stacks' fixed user `jovyan`, one container and one `~/work` volume per Hub user; their only kernel is "Lakehouse (Python 3.10)", and they have `git` and JupyterLab Git.
- **Workload Python environment** (`infra/workload-python/`): one pinned Python 3.10 environment, `/opt/lakehouse/venv`, identical in the Spark runtime and Jupyter images; the rules for a product's `requirements.txt` extras in CI, Airflow runs and Jupyter; and the platform's Spark session module `lakehouse_spark` (`infra/workload-python/python/`, at `/opt/lakehouse/python`, on the venv's path through `lakehouse-platform.pth`), the only copy of the Polaris catalog, token-source and redaction settings. See `functional-design/workload-python-environment.md`.
- **Jenkins** (2.580.1) runs the CI for each data product: a folder per product, whose owner group is its admin, holding `<name>_ci` (prod and UAT branches) and `<name>_cd` (branches with an open pull request) when the product has a `repo`. It uses Keycloak SSO and runs from `compose.jenkins.yml`. See `functional-design/jenkins-ci-access.md`.
- **StarRocks** (4.1.7, one FE and one BE) is the interactive SQL engine.
  - It runs from its own Compose module, `compose.starrocks.yml`, as part of `start`, unless `STARROCKS_ENABLED=false`.
  - It reads and writes the three Polaris catalogs as `srv-starrocks`, with vended RustFS credentials.
  - People log in with their LDAP password; product writers with a Keycloak token. See `functional-design/starrocks-sql-access.md`.
  - Product repositories declare materialized views in `materialized_views/`; the Airflow DAG factory deploys them to UAT and prod as the writer. See `functional-design/materialized-view-promotion.md`.
- **Deferred and retired**: FreeIPA, Hive Metastore, and MIT Kerberos are retired from the target default runtime, as are the FreeIPA-era RustFS identity scripts and the Kerberos, LDAP, and Hive-era StarRocks assets. On 2026-11-09 the following were also removed: the TPC-H generator and loader, the identity provisioner, the old bucket-init image, the one-time catalog path reset, the Ranger test secrets, the Jenkins home migration, the deferred-services inventory, and the root `Jenkinsfile`.

## Repository independence

This repository runs on its own. The only link to workload repositories (today `opensource-lakehouse-sample-dp`, renamed from `opensource-lakehouse` on 2026-11-10, named in each product's `repo` block) is Airflow cloning their Git Bundles anonymously over HTTPS into this repository's `.runtime/airflow-dag-bundles`. No sibling checkout is mounted or referenced, and there is no `LAKEHOUSE_PROJECT_ROOT` setting. The workload repository supplies workflow declarations (`workflows/*.json`), configuration, notebooks, and workload entry points; the platform builds the DAGs (see `functional-design/airflow-workflows.md`). Its own knowledge documents were retired on 2026-10-31.

## Airflow and shared Spark runtime

The Airflow control plane and writer token broker run in the v2 Compose boundary. For each DAG run, Airflow:
1. resolves the selected Git Bundle revision
2. registers run-scoped broker state
3. creates an ephemeral Spark container with the bundle mounted read-only

Each data product with a `repo` has its own writer identity, its `writer_user` (`srv-<name>-writer`, group `role-<name>-writer`; `srv-default-writer` for `default`). There is no writer field: the writer follows from the product name.

- **Selecting the writer**: a DAG ID starts with its bundle name (`<product>-main-...` or `<product>-uat-...`). The broker takes the product from that prefix, then asks the Airflow API, as the read-only FAB user `lakehouse-broker` (role Viewer, recreated by `airflow-init` at every `start-airflow`; Viewer token cached until 60 s before expiry, and when Airflow refuses it with 401 or 403, as it does for a token of the recreated user, the broker signs in again and retries once), which bundle holds the DAG. It issues a token only when `bundle_name` is `<product>-<env>`, and checks that the token's user and writer group are that product's. Refusals are 403 `unknown_product`, `unknown_dag`, or `bundle_mismatch`; 503 when Airflow cannot answer. Registrations keep their product, so renewals use the same writer.
- **Credentials**: the broker gets tokens through the password grant on the confidential `lakehouse-writer` client. `scripts/setup/stage-airflow-writers.py` stages `writers.json` (product → username, group, password file name) and the writers' passwords into `.runtime/container-mounts/airflow-writers/`, which only the broker mounts read-only. The client secret and passwords never reach Airflow DAG code or Spark; Spark receives an initial access token and a run-scoped renewal capability. Polaris sees the product's writer principal.

Per-run execution contract:
1. Airflow resolves a run against the pinned checkout of the product's production or UAT Bundle.
2. The broker checks the DAG's bundle, gets that product's writer token, associates it with that DAG run, and issues a high-entropy, run-scoped renewal capability.
3. Airflow starts one ephemeral Spark container, mounts the Bundle read-only, and passes only the initial token, broker endpoint and CA, run handle, and capability.
4. The Iceberg `AuthManager` renews the token through the broker over authenticated TLS. Polaris enforces the writer role and vends scoped RustFS credentials.
5. On completion or failure, Airflow removes the container and revokes broker run state. Run state also expires on its own.

Broker registration or renewal failures fail the task; there is no fallback identity.

The shared runtime uses Spark 3.5.5, Java 17, and Iceberg 1.10.2. Its JVM `AuthManager` renews access tokens through identity-specific adapters: Airflow uses the run-scoped writer broker, and Jupyter Spark uses the authenticated user's Hub broker. Both start their session through `lakehouse_spark.create_spark_session(app_name, catalog)`, which chooses the adapter from the process environment and never falls back from one to the other; product repositories pass only their config's `catalog_name`. These identities and capabilities are not interchangeable. Polaris remains the authorization and scoped RustFS credential vending point for all table data; no RustFS root credential is handed to Spark. The only static RustFS credentials Spark receives are checkpoint keys (see [Streaming checkpoints](#streaming-checkpoints)).

**Bundles come from the product files.** Every product with a `repo` block (`url`: credential-free https; `prod_branch`; `uat_branch`) gets two GitDagBundles, `<name>-main` tracking its prod branch and `<name>-uat` tracking its UAT branch (`git_conn_id` `lakehouse_git`, refresh 300 s, sparse `dags`, `workflows`, `notebooks`, `configs`, and `subdir` `dags`, so Airflow looks for DAG files only in `dags/`; root files such as `requirements.txt` are always checked out). Airflow applies `sparse_dirs` only at the first clone, so `scripts/setup/sync-bundle-checkouts.py`, run by `start-airflow` before Airflow starts, updates existing `tracking_repo` checkouts. `default` has `default-main` and `default-uat` from `opensource-lakehouse-sample-dp` (`main`, `uat`); the former `lakehouse-main`/`lakehouse-uat` names are retired. `scripts/setup/airflow-bundle-config.py` generates the list (`data_products.bundle_config`), and `infra/airflow/validate-bundle-config.py` checks its shape; with `--host-paths`, which `scripts/lakehouse.sh` passes, it also requires equality with the generated list and that the host Bundle root is this repository's `.runtime/airflow-dag-bundles`. The copy inside the image checks only the shape.

**Workload contract.** A product repository declares DAGs only in `workflows/<name>.json` or, grouped by subproject, `workflows/<project>/<name>.json` (workflow JSON v1; entry points in `notebooks/workload/<project>/`, optionally in a layer folder `bronze`, `silver`, `gold`, `ops`, `deploy` or `other`; names unique per repository) and keeps the fixed stub `dags/lakehouse.py`; it no longer contains DAG code. The platform builds `<bundle>-<name>` with `create_cluster`, `install_requirements` (the repository's optional root `requirements.txt`, constrained by the workload lock, into the run's container), `validate_environment` (the repository's `config_loader`, run inside the Spark container), `submit_<task>` per task (`args` after `--`, optional retries and timeouts), `stop_cluster`, and `verify_workloads_succeeded`. No product repository code runs in the scheduler, which holds the Docker socket and the broker control token, none outside `dags/` is parsed by the DAG processor, and no task renders templates. Workload code runs on the shared Python 3.10 environment plus the repository's extras. The repository's `configs/<product>/<env>.yml` is read before `configs/<env>.yml`, and Jenkins checks the workflows and `requirements.txt` with `lakehouse-validate-workflows`. `opensource-lakehouse-sample-dp` follows this since `9cbd6f8` (2026-11-10), with extras (`duckdb==1.5.6`) and the `generate_tpch` workflow since `8ef716f`; its earlier in-repository factory (`fedf0bc`) is retired.

**Airflow restarts.** Airflow 3.3 reads `dag_bundle_config_list` once per process (`DagBundlesManager`), from an environment variable, and the broker reads its writers at start. So a change to the bundles or writers recreates Airflow, interrupting running DAG runs (LocalExecutor). A fingerprint over the bundle list, the writer set, and password hashes (`stage-airflow-writers.py --fingerprint`) is recorded in `.runtime/state/airflow-bundles.json` after a successful `start-airflow`; the product commands recreate Airflow only when it differs and Airflow is running. Alternatives (broker hot reload with idle-only restart; one local platform bundle; other orchestrators) were discussed on 2026-11-09 and not adopted. The writer client has a one-hour access-token lifetime override; human JupyterHub token lifetimes remain unchanged.

## Streaming checkpoints

Spark Structured Streaming jobs keep durable checkpoints in their product's own environment bucket, under `checkpoints/`, in Airflow runs and in Jupyter (since 2026-11-11). Details: `functional-design/workload-python-environment.md` (session settings and the product contract), `functional-design/lakehouse-product-access.md` (keys, policies, delivery by role, rotation), `functional-design/airflow-workflows.md` (the run container's key).

**Constraints found by probing (2026-11-11)**:
1. The images had no Hadoop S3 filesystem.
2. Polaris vends credentials only for table locations.
3. Iceberg 1.10.2's streaming source reads and writes `<checkpoint>/sources/0/offsets/0` through the **source table's** FileIO (`InitialOffsetStore` uses `Table.io()`), so with `S3FileIO` any checkpoint outside the table location gets 403. Iceberg PR #18092 only moves that code; no release changes it.
4. RustFS 1.0.4 STS (`AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`) accepts only tokens whose every audience is trusted, and it trusts only `rustfs`, so the job's own Polaris token is refused.

**Design**:
- **Routing**: every Polaris catalog uses Iceberg's built-in `ResolvingFileIO`. It sends `s3`, `s3a`, `s3n` to `S3FileIO` with vended credentials (prefix and bulk operations and storage credentials kept) and other schemes to `HadoopFileIO`. Checkpoints use the dedicated scheme `s3ckpt://`, mapped to S3A (`hadoop-aws` 3.3.4 and the AWS SDK v1 bundle 1.12.262 in the runtime image). `s3://` and `s3a://` stay unmapped, so table paths never reach S3A. No custom FileIO.
- **Credentials**: one static key per product environment bucket, RustFS user `ckpt-<bucket>` with only the policy `checkpoints-<bucket>`, created by the product bootstrap (`infra/rustfs/bootstrap-checkpoint-keys.py`), stored in `.runtime/credentials/` and staged as files. This is the one bounded exception to "workloads never receive static RustFS credentials": non-root, one bucket, one prefix, no table data.
- **Delivery**: an Airflow run container mounts only its own product environment's key (`prod` or `uat`); a Jupyter server mounts the `dev` keys of the user's owner or developer products, never `uat` or `prod`; analysts get none. `lakehouse_spark` sets S3A per-bucket keys and no global key, so several products work in one kernel and any other bucket fails closed.
- **Contract**: products set `checkpoint_path: s3ckpt://<bucket>/checkpoints` in `configs/<env>.yml`.

**Alternatives considered**:
- **STS with the job's own token** (the first requirement): proven to work with a Keycloak standard token exchange to an `aud=rustfs` token and a session policy limited to `checkpoints/`. It needs the exchange in both brokers and a JVM S3A credentials provider with renewal (credentials last at most an hour). Not chosen because it is the most custom runtime code; it remains the upgrade path, changing only the platform's S3A credential settings, not products' paths or notebooks.
- **Checkpoints inside table folders**: the target table's folder fails (offsets are written with the source's credentials), and the source's folder would be deleted by orphan-file cleanup or a table drop and fails for read-only sources.
- **A FUSE mount of the bucket** (the old Databricks mount pattern): needs host-level FUSE or a volume plugin, emulates renames with copy and delete, and still needs a static key; rejected.
- **A custom routing FileIO in Java**: unnecessary, since `ResolvingFileIO` already routes by scheme.
- **Snapshot bookkeeping instead of streaming**: would work for Iceberg sources only and would not serve future streaming jobs.

**Accepted limits**: shared keys per product environment (code in a Jupyter server can read its dev keys; a notebook and a dev stream with the same path share the checkpoint, accepted because dev is a sandbox); manual rotation with restarts; membership changes at the next server start; about 280 MB more per image; streams from Iceberg tables with delete or overwrite snapshots need the `streaming-skip-*` options; S3 renames are not atomic, so one writer per checkpoint.

**Follow-up**: propose upstream that Iceberg write `offsets/0` through the checkpoint's Hadoop filesystem, which would make the dedicated scheme unnecessary.

## Airflow browser authentication

The Airflow API server uses FAB OIDC with the confidential `airflow` client in the Keycloak `lakehouse` realm.

- **Endpoints**: browser authorization uses the host-reachable Keycloak hostname; token and user-info requests use Docker networking.
- **Token validation**: the configured issuer is validated explicitly. The RS256 JWKS is fetched from the internal Keycloak service address, so Docker loopback resolution does not send the request back to Airflow.
- **Callbacks**: the exact local callback URLs are `http://localhost:8085/auth/oauth-authorized/keycloak` and `http://127.0.0.1:8085/auth/oauth-authorized/keycloak`.
- **Exposure and recovery**: the Airflow service stays loopback-bound. The local FAB password login is a separate recovery route restricted to `AIRFLOW_ADMIN_USERNAME`.

**Role mapping** (since 2026-11-09):
- At each sign-in, `LakehouseSecurityManager` maps the user's groups to Airflow roles from every product file's `apps.airflow`, with `role-platform-admin` always `Admin`. `AUTH_ROLES_MAPPING` is a fixed identity map of the three role names.
- The API server mounts the product model and `data-products/` read-only. Other Airflow services load the module without importing the model.
- Airflow has no per-product permissions, so these roles apply platform-wide.
- An invalid product file fails closed: only the platform administrator signs in.

| Group (default product file) | Airflow role |
|---|---|
| `role-default-owner` | `User` |
| `role-default-developer` | `User` |
| `role-default-analyst` | `User` |
| `role-default-writer` | `Viewer` |
| `role-platform-admin` | `Admin` |

Users without a mapped group are denied OAuth login. The Airflow OIDC integration is browser-only and does not change API or service-account authentication.

Only `role-platform-admin` is Airflow `Admin`. Owners and developers are `User` (decided 2026-11-09; supersedes the Airflow SSO intent's `Admin` for owners and developers). Roles sync at every sign-in (`AUTH_ROLES_SYNC_AT_LOGIN`).

## RustFS console authentication

**Login flow**
- The RustFS console offers Keycloak sign-in through the confidential `rustfs` client in the `lakehouse` realm: Authorization Code with PKCE S256.
- The callback is derived from the browser host: `http://{localhost,127.0.0.1}:<console port>/rustfs/admin/v3/oidc/callback/default`. The console port is `RUSTFS_CONSOLE_HOST_PORT`, default 9001.
- Keycloak registers exactly those two callbacks, plus the post-logout URIs `.../rustfs/console/auth/login`. RustFS rejects static loopback redirect URIs, so the exact Keycloak list is the allowlist. Logins started on the S3 port fail at Keycloak.

**Reaching Keycloak**
- Keycloak advertises `keycloak.localhost:8080` for token, JWKS, and logout endpoints, and that name resolves to loopback inside containers.
- RustFS therefore reaches Keycloak over the internal network `lakehouse-local_rustfs-identity`, where Keycloak carries the alias `keycloak.localhost`. No other service joins that network.
- `RUSTFS_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_ORIGINS` allows exactly `http://keycloak.localhost:8080`.
- The `lakehouse-rustfs-groups` mapper puts `groups` in the ID token.

**Client secret**
- The secret is `.runtime/credentials/rustfs-oidc-client-secret`.
- `infra/rustfs/rustfs-entrypoint.sh` exports it into the RustFS process at start, because RustFS 1.0.4 has no file-based OIDC secret setting.
- It is absent from Compose files and `docker inspect`.

**Authorization and sessions**
- RustFS uses each `groups` value as a policy name. Each product's group policies and the aggregate `role-platform-admin` policy are described in `functional-design/lakehouse-product-access.md`.
- Users with no matching policy are refused a session. Console sessions last one hour.
- Logout is RP-initiated through Keycloak.
- If Keycloak is unavailable, new OIDC logins fail, existing sessions run to expiry, and RustFS retries discovery.

**Root and Polaris**: root static keys remain the break-glass console login and the identity Polaris uses server-side for STS.

**Known upstream limitation**: RustFS 1.0.4 embeds console v0.1.37. Its bucket-list page (`/rustfs/console/browser/`) remounts in a loop for non-admin users, which includes every OIDC user ([rustfs/console#271](https://github.com/rustfs/console/issues/271); fixed in console v0.1.38). Users open a bucket directly at `/rustfs/console/browser?bucket=<name>`. Follow-up: adopt the first RustFS release that bundles console v0.1.38 or later, and re-check the console's metadata-action needs.

## Jenkins CI authentication

**Service**
- Jenkins runs as the service `jenkins` in `compose.jenkins.yml` on `127.0.0.1:${JENKINS_HOST_PORT:-8090}`, unless `JENKINS_ENABLED=false`.
- Its home is `lakehouse-local_jenkins-home`, which holds the build history. Folders and jobs are configuration as code (see below) and are recreated at every start, also after a reset.

**Plugins**
- The image pins exactly 105 plugins in `infra/jenkins/plugins.txt`: the legacy versions plus `oic-auth 4.731.v4932b_506e767`, `nimbus-jose-jwt-api`, and `job-dsl 3732.v9a_c49a_61a_313`.
- The build compares `name:version` from every plugin manifest and fails on any mismatch, and `PLUGINS_FORCE_UPGRADE=true` makes the image authoritative over the home's plugins.

**Configuration as code**
- `infra/jenkins/casc/jenkins.yaml` is the template: the OIDC realm, the project-based matrix with its static entries (`role-platform-admin`, `jenkins-break-glass`), the escape hatch, executors, mode, crumb issuer, and root URL.
- `infra/products/render_jenkins.py` writes three files to `.runtime/container-mounts/`: `jenkins-casc.yaml` (the template plus `Overall/Read` per product group), `jenkins-jobs.groovy` (Job DSL: product folders with their permissions and jobs), and `jenkins-products.json` (the expected folders and jobs).
  - The init hook `infra/jenkins/init.groovy.d/reconcile-data-products.groovy` applies the Job DSL after Jenkins has loaded its jobs, then deletes the marked product folders and jobs that left the expected set. A Job DSL script in CasC would run before job loading and lose new folders.
  - `prepare-runtime.py` renders the files on `start`, and the operator scripts render them and restart Jenkins when one changed.
  - The files are rewritten in place, because a single-file bind mount keeps its inode.
- Endpoints follow the Airflow pattern: browser redirects use `keycloak.localhost:8080`; token, JWKS, and userinfo calls use `keycloak:8080`; the issuer is the canonical one. No network alias is needed.

**Keycloak client and secrets**
- The confidential `jenkins` client uses PKCE S256, exact `finishLogin` callbacks and `/` post-logout URIs for both loopback hosts, and a `groups` claim in the ID token (`lakehouse-jenkins-groups`).
- The client secret and the escape-hatch password are protected files read through `${trim:${readFile:...}}`.

**Builds**: pipelines run on the built-in node without the Docker socket. GitHub is scanned anonymously.

## Resource and data role model

Every data product has three environments in the **shared** Polaris catalogs, each with its own namespace, bucket, and StarRocks MV database. The `default` product:

| Environment | Catalog | Namespace | Bucket |
|---|---|---|---|
| Production | `lakehouse` | `default_lh` | `bucket-default` |
| UAT | `lakehouse_uat` | `default_lhuat` | `bucket-default-uat` |
| Dev | `lakehouse_dev` | `default_lhdev` | `bucket-default-dev` |

- **Paths**: each catalog's default base location is the default product's `<bucket>/<catalog>/`. Its allowed locations add `s3://<bucket>/<catalog>/` for every product.
- **Namespace locations**: a product's namespace has the location `s3://<bucket>/<catalog>/<namespace>/`, so tables resolve beneath `<bucket>/<catalog>/<namespace>/<table>`. For example, the production smoke table is `s3://bucket-default/lakehouse/default_lh/bootstrap_smoke_test/`.
- **Polaris flag**: a namespace outside the catalog's base bucket needs the server-wide Polaris feature `ALLOW_NAMESPACE_CUSTOM_LOCATION` (set in `infra/polaris/oidc.properties`). Polaris 1.8 ignores the per-catalog property and the `behavior-changes` form. Tables stay confined to the allowed locations.
- **OIDC filter**: it is the pattern `^role-[a-z][a-z0-9]{1,19}-(developer|analyst|owner|writer)$`, so new products need no Polaris restart.

Role semantics, Polaris grants, and RustFS console policies are described in `functional-design/lakehouse-product-access.md`. Polaris enforces catalog operations. Polaris-vended credentials constrain object access for workloads, and the group-named RustFS policies constrain direct console access. These data-platform privileges are distinct from the Airflow UI role mapping above. StarRocks adds its own role layer on top of Polaris (see `functional-design/starrocks-sql-access.md`).

## Data products

- **Configuration**: one YAML file per product in `data-products/` (`apiVersion: lakehouse.local/v1`). The file holds the environments, groups, access levels (none, read, write, manage), MV levels (none, read, author, manage), app mappings, and writer user.
- **Validation**: names, the group pattern `role-<token>-<role>`, the shared catalogs, collisions across files, and unknown keys. Names are locked once applied: `.runtime/state/data-products/<name>.json` records them.
- **Component interface**: every product-aware component script takes `--product FILE` (default: every file), `--dry-run`, and, where it holds data or members, `--inventory` and `--remove [--purge-data]`. Each script remains the only writer to its system.
- **Operator commands** (`scripts/operations/`):
  - `create-data-product.sh`: `--init <name>`; apply `<file>` with `[--dry-run] [--no-restart]`. Order: validate, Keycloak, RustFS, Polaris, Polaris sync, StarRocks, StarRocks sync, Jenkins render (folder, permissions, jobs), record state, Airflow.
  - `remove-data-product.sh <name> [--purge-data] [--yes] [--dry-run]`: refuses `default`, inventories, asks for the typed name, backs up to `.runtime/backups/<time>-remove-<name>/`, then removes in reverse order (Jenkins folder and entries, StarRocks, Polaris roles, Polaris namespaces and locations, RustFS, Keycloak). It syncs and deletes the file, then updates Airflow, so a failed run resumes.
  - `create-user.sh <username> …`: one enabled user, no groups.
  - **Admin sign-in**: all three sign in to the Keycloak `lakehouse` realm as a platform administrator (`--admin-user`, `--admin-password-file`, `LAKEHOUSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, or a hidden prompt; never an argument) and refuse non-members of `role-platform-admin`. Polaris, RustFS, and StarRocks use the protected bootstrap credentials.
- **Concurrency**: a lock directory, `.runtime/state/data-products/.lock`, allows one create or remove at a time.
- **Restarts**: Jenkins when its configuration, folders, or jobs change (the dry run prints the folders and jobs to create or delete), and Airflow when the bundles or writers change (a product with a `repo` created or removed, or its `repo` changed): `apply_airflow` in `scripts/operations/lib/data-products.sh` runs `start-airflow` when the fingerprint differs and Airflow is running (`--no-restart` prints the command; `--dry-run` lists the bundles). Sign-in mappings need no restart: JupyterHub, Airflow, and the scheduled sync read the mounted files.

## Compose modules

One Compose project, `lakehouse-local`, split into module files. Resource names are the same as in the former single `docker-compose.yml`.

| File | Services | Selected by |
|---|---|---|
| `compose.core.yml` | keycloak-db, keycloak, ldap, polaris-db, polaris-schema-init, polaris, polaris-group-reconciler, rustfs; networks core, data-access, rustfs-identity | always |
| `compose.jupyter.yml` | jupyterhub; network jupyter-user; volume jupyterhub-state | `JUPYTER_ENABLED` (default true) |
| `compose.jenkins.yml` | jenkins; volume jenkins-home | `JENKINS_ENABLED` (default true) |
| `compose.starrocks.yml` | starrocks-fe, starrocks-be; network starrocks | `STARROCKS_ENABLED` (default true) |
| `compose.airflow.yml` | Airflow and its token broker; networks airflow-internal, airflow-spark | the `start-airflow`, `airflow-status`, and `stop-airflow` commands |

- **One file list**: `scripts/lakehouse.sh` reads the flags from the environment or `.env` (case-insensitive) and builds `COMPOSE` (core plus enabled modules) and `AIRFLOW_COMPOSE` (that plus Airflow) in one place. Every other script passes its files explicitly, and no command relies on a default Compose file.
- **Reproducible builds**: both entry scripts export `BUILDX_NO_DEFAULT_ATTESTATIONS=1`. With the containerd image store, BuildKit otherwise adds a timestamped attestation, so every cached build gets a new image ID and running containers are recreated on each start.
- **Orphans**: both entry scripts export `COMPOSE_IGNORE_ORPHANS=true`. A command that passes only some module files would otherwise label the other modules' containers orphans and suggest `--remove-orphans`, which deletes them.

## Startup and bootstrap

**Start.** `scripts/lakehouse.sh start`:
1. creates only missing protected runtime credentials (`scripts/setup/prepare-runtime.py`), including the LDAP admin and bind passwords, the Hub maintenance token, the LDAP and StarRocks TLS material, and Keycloak's `truststore-paths`; builds the shared Spark runtime image
2. if Jupyter is enabled: prepares the Hub broker certificates, checks the user subnet and credentials, and builds the Hub and single-user images
3. starts the core databases, RustFS, and `ldap` (built from `infra/ldap/`), runs the Polaris schema initialization, then starts Keycloak (which waits for `ldap` and trusts its CA) and Polaris, and waits for health
4. runs the Keycloak realm bootstrap:
   - it first ensures and tests the `lakehouse-ldap` provider, so every user created afterwards lands in LDAP
   - it creates `role-platform-admin`, every product's groups (from `data-products/`), the clients, and any missing bootstrap users
   - it gives `role-platform-admin` the `lakehouse` realm's `realm-admin` role, and never changes an existing user
5. starts each enabled module (JupyterHub, Jenkins, StarRocks with its TLS material and runtime bootstrap), and prints a notice for each disabled one

**Product bootstrap.** `scripts/bootstrap-default-product.sh` provisions provider resources and grants for **every** product file (`default` first), then records the applied names:
1. reruns `start` and the realm bootstrap, then `scripts/bootstrap/bootstrap-users.sh`, which resets the five bootstrap users to their default password and single group
2. creates the buckets, then the RustFS group policies
3. creates catalogs and grants, and reconciles memberships
4. verifies writer authentication
5. runs Spark smoke-table create/write/read checks (`scripts/bootstrap/smoke-spark.sh`) on the shared runtime image `local/lakehouse-spark-runtime:3.5.5_1.10.2`, with explicit OAuth2 catalog authentication
6. runs the StarRocks bootstrap and user reconcile

Reruns preserve bucket objects and do not duplicate smoke rows. The realm and policy bootstraps refuse conflicting existing configuration. The only automatic change to existing configuration is narrow: a policy that exactly equals its previous approved definition is upgraded. `scripts/verify/rustfs-oidc.py` and `scripts/verify/jenkins-oidc.py` check the RustFS and Jenkins OIDC wiring read-only. `scripts/lakehouse.sh stop` stops the enabled modules and core, and preserves named volumes.

**Reset.** `scripts/lakehouse.sh reset` (`scripts/operations/reset-lakehouse.py`) deletes all local platform state:
- `lakehouse-local` containers, plus Jupyter user servers and Airflow Spark runs by runtime-role label
- the nine data volumes (including StarRocks and `ldap-data`) and the `lakehouse-jupyter-home-*` volumes
- the seven networks (including `lakehouse-local_starrocks`)
- `.runtime/credentials`, `.runtime/container-mounts`, `.runtime/airflow-dag-bundles`, and `.runtime/state` (the applied product names)

It lists what it will delete first. The product files in `data-products/` are kept, and the rebuild recreates every product with empty buckets. It needs the typed word `reset`, or `--yes`, and `--dry-run` only lists. A path guard refuses symlinks and other paths. Images, other projects, other `.runtime` entries such as `backups`, and anything outside the repository are kept. It is irreversible, and a rebuild is `bootstrap-default-product.sh`.

**Airflow.** `scripts/lakehouse.sh start-airflow`:
1. prepares Airflow secrets (including the broker's Viewer password) and certificates
2. stages the product writers and generates and validates the bundle list
3. additively bootstraps the Keycloak Airflow client and group mapper
4. builds the Airflow images and starts the control plane (`airflow-init` recreates the `lakehouse-broker` Viewer); recreates the broker when the fingerprint changed
5. waits for service readiness
6. waits for DAGs from every product bundle (`scripts/verify/airflow-dags.sh`), warning about DAG IDs without their bundle prefix, without running DAGs
7. records the fingerprint

`scripts/lakehouse.sh stop-airflow` stops Airflow services and Spark runs while preserving provider data, Airflow metadata, and Bundle checkouts. Keycloak clients and mappers are persistent realm configuration and are not removed by stopping services.

**Secrets.** All published host endpoints bind to loopback. Protected credentials remain under `.runtime/credentials/` and must be backed up separately using encrypted storage. No secrets belong in source control, reports, or command output.

## StarRocks SQL engine

**Runtime**
- `compose.starrocks.yml` holds `starrocks-fe` and `starrocks-be`. The upstream `starrocks/fe-ubuntu` and `be-ubuntu` 4.1.7 images are pinned by multi-arch digest, with no custom build.
- **Ports**: SQL on 9030 and HTTP on 8030, bound to loopback.
- **Networks**: `core` (Keycloak, Polaris, the scheduled reconciler), `data-access` (RustFS), and an internal `lakehouse-local_starrocks`.
- **Volumes**: `starrocks-fe-meta` and `starrocks-be-storage`.
- **Memory**: `STARROCKS_FE_MEMORY_LIMIT` (default 2g; FE heap 1280 MB) and `STARROCKS_BE_MEMORY_LIMIT` (default 4g).
- **Config**: the tracked `infra/starrocks/conf/{fe,be}.conf` is mounted read-only. `infra/starrocks/fe-entrypoint.sh` adds the TLS keystore settings from protected files.
  - **Forced TLS**: `fe.conf` sets `ssl_force_secure_transport = true`, so every MySQL-protocol connection must use TLS.
  - **LDAP**: LDAPS to `ldap:636`, verified with the LDAP CA mounted at `/run/certs/ldap-ca.crt`.
  - **Bind pattern**: `uid=${USER},ou=people,…` is a runtime setting. `fe.conf` would expand `${USER}` as an environment variable and the FE would refuse to start, so it is set by the runtime bootstrap and re-applied by every user sync.

**Lifecycle**
- `scripts/lakehouse.sh` adds `compose.starrocks.yml` to the module file list when enabled (see [Compose modules](#compose-modules)).
- `start` prepares the TLS material, starts FE and BE, and runs `bootstrap-starrocks.py --runtime-only` (root password once, BE registration, LDAP bind pattern).
- The product bootstrap runs `bootstrap-starrocks.py` (catalogs, MV databases, roles) and `reconcile-starrocks-users.py`.
- `status` and `stop` include StarRocks, and `reconcile-starrocks [--dry-run]` runs the user sync on demand.
- The reset removes both StarRocks volumes and the network.

**Identities**
- **Catalog identity**: the confidential Keycloak client `srv-starrocks`, whose service account is in every product's writer group. Its Polaris principal, `service-account-srv-starrocks`, is created by the existing group reconciler.
- **People and service users**: they log in with their own username and LDAP password (`authentication_ldap_simple`); the FE binds to LDAP as the user and holds no LDAP secret. The former token login, with the `starrocks` Keycloak client and `starrocks-token.sh`, was retired on 2026-11-09.
- **Secrets**: the root password, the `srv-starrocks` secret, and the TLS keys live in `.runtime/credentials`. The keystore and its password are staged read-only in `.runtime/container-mounts`.

**Interfaces**
- **Iceberg REST**: `http://polaris:8181/api/catalog` with OAuth2 client credentials against `http://keycloak:8080/.../token`, `scope=openid`, and vended credentials.
- **LDAP**: `ldaps://ldap:636`, binding as `uid=<user>,ou=people,dc=lakehouse,dc=local`.
- **SQL and JDBC**: username and password over TLS from the local StarRocks CA.
  - **CLI**: `scripts/clients/starrocks-login.sh` (MySQL 9.7 client, cleartext plugin, `VERIFY_IDENTITY`).
  - **JDBC, DBeaver, and BI tools**: username and password with `sslMode=REQUIRED` or `VERIFY_IDENTITY`. Connector/J 9.3.0 was verified, and a plain-text connection is refused.
- **Scheduled sync**: its MariaDB client connects with `--ssl --ssl-verify-server-cert` and the StarRocks CA.

- While `ldap` is down, Keycloak sign-ins of federated users and StarRocks password logins fail; client service accounts, issued tokens, and open sessions keep working. LDAP is a single local node.
- After an FE restart outside `lakehouse.sh start`, StarRocks password logins fail until the next user sync re-applies the bind pattern (at most five minutes).
- `lakehouse.sh start` replaces staged files in `.runtime/container-mounts/` atomically; running containers with single-file mounts see the new content only after a restart.
- This local single-node setup is not a production, HA, or multi-host certification.

# Functional Design — Materialized View Promotion

Current design of how StarRocks materialized views travel from a product's dev MV database to UAT and production. Related: [`airflow-workflows.md`](airflow-workflows.md) (where the deploy runs), [`starrocks-sql-access.md`](starrocks-sql-access.md) (MV databases, writer login).

## Responsibility
Developers build and test views by hand in the dev MV database; the product repository declares them; the platform deploys them in UAT (`<product>-uat` bundle) and production (`<product>-main` bundle) as the product's writer, so views reach production through reviewed branches like code.

## Definitions (`lakehouse_dags.spec`, also run by Jenkins)
- `materialized_views/<project>/<name>.sql`; the file name is the view name: lowercase letters, digits and single `_`, at most 60 characters (no `__`: the deployer reserves `<name>__lakehouse_new`). Names are unique across subprojects.
- One statement: `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ${mv_database}.<file name> ...`; leading `--` lines and a trailing `;` are ignored; any other `;` is refused. Only `${catalog}`, `${namespace}` and `${mv_database}` may appear; at most 100 000 bytes.
- The workflow name `deploy_materialized_views` is reserved.

## Deploy (`lakehouse_dags.mv_deploy`, `factory._deploy_materialized_views`)
- **Where**: every workflow DAG of a bundle with view files runs `deploy_materialized_views` after `validate_environment` and before its tasks (its failure stops the tasks; `stop_cluster` still runs); `<bundle>-deploy_materialized_views` runs it on demand and revokes its broker run afterwards. One task covers all views.
- **Values**: the scheduler reads the environment's `catalog`, `namespace` and `mv_database`, and `writer_user.username`, from the product file (`LAKEHOUSE_DATA_PRODUCTS_DIR`).
- **Login**: re-registering the run with the broker (control token) returns a fresh writer access token, bundle-checked by the broker; the deploy logs in to StarRocks (`starrocks-fe:9030`, TLS, `/run/certs/starrocks-ca.crt`) as the writer with that token through a client handler for `authentication_openid_connect_client`. The token is never logged or given to product code. `STARROCKS_ENABLED=false` skips the deploy with a warning.
- **Marker**: each deployed view's comment starts with `lakehouse-mv sha256=<first 16 hex of SHA-256 of the rendered statement>`, followed by the file's own comment.
- **Plan** (existing views read from `information_schema.materialized_views` and `tables`):
  - no view with a file's name -> create;
  - managed view, same digest -> unchanged (no SQL);
  - managed view, other digest -> replace: drop any leftover `<name>__lakehouse_new`, create it with the new definition, `ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW <name> SWAP WITH <name>__lakehouse_new` (atomic), drop the staging name (now the old view);
  - managed view without a file -> drop;
  - a view without the marker -> never changed; reported if a file has its name.
- **Errors**: a create or replace failing with "Unknown table" (5502) is skipped (a later run creates it); any other failure is reported, the other views continue, and the task fails at the end naming the failed views; a failed replace leaves the current view.
- **Log**: `Materialized views in <db>: created [...], replaced [...], dropped [...], unchanged [...], skipped (source table missing) [...], made by hand [...], failed [...]`.

## Testable properties
- Deploying twice converges: after one apply the managed views equal the files (by digest), hand-made views are untouched, and a second apply creates, replaces and drops nothing (Hypothesis, `tests/airflow/test_mv_promotion.py`).

## Limits
- A changed view is rebuilt from scratch: until its first refresh it is empty for direct reads, and rewrite falls back to the base tables. User decision: no synchronous refresh before the swap.
- Query rewrite needs SPJG views (no subqueries), freshness, and rollable aggregates (`SUM` yes, `COUNT(DISTINCT)` no).
- StarRocks' trace may keep listing `<name>__lakehouse_new` as related to the base tables after a swap (stale label; the view resolves by ID).
- Dev has no deploy: developers create dev views by hand.
